---
title: "Legitimacy, trust & compliance"
toc: true
---

## Motivation (stylized facts)
::: {.callout-note title="Stylized facts this mechanism aims to match"}
- Reporting and cooperation vary with trust in institutions.
- Enforcement can backfire if it reduces perceived legitimacy (lower cooperation).
:::

## Mechanism
Legitimacy affects:
- willingness to report victimization,
- willingness to cooperate as witness,
- voluntary compliance with rules.

This can be modeled as:
- a participation constraint (report/cooperate only if expected benefit exceeds cost),
- a utility component (disutility from cooperating with an illegitimate authority),
- or a belief channel (expectations of fair treatment).

## Canonical modeling primitives
- reporting stage: victim decides to report; police decide effort; offender anticipates
- informational asymmetry: police need community cooperation to identify offenders
- dynamic trust: policies today affect future cooperation

## Predictions (qualitative)
- higher legitimacy increases reporting and clearance rates (even holding incidence fixed)
- aggressive policies can reduce cooperation, lowering detection and potentially increasing incidence in the long run
- measured crime can rise when trust improves (more reporting), even if incidence falls

## Later-on analysis
- links naturally to signaling and dynamic games (reputation of institutions)
- connects to “recorded vs incidence” measurement: reporting is endogenous
